gaps.feature: Same-site /api proxy forwards the client's IP and forwarding headers to the API (the edge proxy in saas-base)
gaps.detail: Checked and confirmed. In /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/apps/web/vite.config.ts, apiProxyRules (/api/**, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/**, /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/**) are plain string targets `{ proxy: `${apiOrigin}/...` }` with no `xfwd`. Nitro 3.0.260903-beta passes them to h3's rule handler (h3/dist/rules/proxy.mjs), which calls proxyRequest(event, target, { ...options }). h3 2.0.8 proxyRequest (dist/proxy.mjs:120) applies applyXForwardedHeaders only when opts.xfwd is set, so the web server adds no x-forwarded-for, x-forwarded-host or x-forwarded-proto. Nitro's own `xfwd: true` default (dist/_dev.mjs createHTTPProxy) is a different dev HTTP proxy and does not cover routeRules. Better Auth in packages/auth/src/auth.ts reads ipAddressHeaders ['x-real-ip','x-forwarded-for'], so behind this proxy, with no upstream edge setting those headers, sessions are stored without an IP and the rate limit has no per-client key. Redirects are already passed through (h3 uses manual redirect). Nothing in the repo tests forwarding (no test outside packages/auth mentions forwarded/x-real-ip), and e2e/smoke only checks that /api is reachable. Fix: use `{ proxy: { to: `${apiOrigin}/api/**`, xfwd: true } }` on all three rules, and add a test asserting the API receives x-forwarded-for, the cookie and the Origin, and that a 302 comes back unfollowed.

gaps.feature: Invitation resend: a failed 'mark email sent' write after the email went out
gaps.detail: Confirmed. In apps/api/src/routers/invitations.ts the resend handler calls `const marked = await context.scope.members.markEmailSent(invitation.id)` after sendInviteMail, and that call is not in a try/catch. invite wraps the same call and still returns emailSent:true. So if the write fails during resend, the request returns a 500 even though the email already went out, and the admin may retry and send a second email. apps/api/src/routers/members.test.ts tests resend only for 404/403/503; nothing makes markEmailSent fail.
gaps.saasBaseRef: apps/api/src/app/members/invitations.controller.ts markSent() used by both invite() and resend()

gaps.feature: Account settings: name of a person who has none
gaps.detail: Confirmed. The accountView in apps/api/src/routers/account.ts returns `name: account.user.name` as is. apps/web/src/components/settings/account-section.tsx fills the field with `draftName ?? account.name`, so for a person with no name the field is empty. Only the avatar falls back, through initialOf(account.name || account.email). The displayName() helper in apps/web/src/lib/current-user.ts would cover this, but only members-section and the current user use it. saas-base toAccount fills the field with displayName(name, email), which falls back to the part of the email before the @.

gaps.feature: Account settings: saving the browser's time zone automatically when it fails
gaps.detail: Confirmed. In account-section.tsx, when account.timeZone === null an effect calls saveRef.current({ timeZone: zone }), which goes through save(). If that save fails, save() calls reportError, shows the toast toastError(t('...notSaved')) and runs reload(). The user sees an error toast for a save they never started. In saas-base, withBrowserZone() only calls errorHandler.handleError and keeps the account as it was, with no toast. No test covers this failure.

gaps.feature: Deleting an organization cascades through every table with organization_id
gaps.detail: Confirmed. packages/db/src/schema.test.ts only checks that each table has a NOT NULL organization_id column. packages/db/src/organization/tenant-db.test.ts uses its own probe table, created with on delete cascade inside the test. No test goes through the real schema tables to check that every organization_id FK is ON DELETE CASCADE, or that deleting an organization leaves no rows behind. The schema is correct today: organizations.ts and usage.ts use onDelete 'cascade'. But nothing would catch a new table that lacks it.

gaps.feature: Plans page: a paying organization counts as paying only when its billing has a known cycle
gaps.detail: Confirmed. In arrakit/apps/web/src/components/billing/plans-page.tsx L58, `const paying = wantsBilling && billing.data ? billing.data : null` never checks `billing.data.cycle`. The contract declares `cycle: billingCycleSchema.nullable()` (packages/contract/src/billing.ts L17), so the null case can happen. When cycle is null, actionFor still offers 'Switch to …' on every paid card. That includes the organization's own plan whenever the isCurrent check depends on the cycle matching. saas-base returns early when `!billing.cycle` (plans.page.ts L126), so it shows no Switch buttons. The fix is to set paying only when billing.data.cycle is non-null and the plan is pro or team. A plans-page test for this case should be added too.

gaps.feature: Billing refusals in the API's own words on Checkout and the plan switch (502/503)
gaps.detail: Confirmed. In arrakit/apps/web/src/components/billing/api-refusal.ts, billingRefusal only passes through statuses 400, 402, 403 and 409 (REFUSALS set). The API does throw SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE 'Payments are not set up yet.' and BAD_GATEWAY with refusal messages (apps/api/src/billing/billing-service.ts L37/L42/L99, orpc/context.ts L89). checkout-page.tsx L50/L66 and plans-page.tsx change.onError therefore show the generic checkout.openFailed and plans.switchFailed texts instead. saas-base uses bodyMessage(error) for any status on these two screens (checkout.page.ts L81, plans.page.ts L153). The fix is a variant, used only for checkout and the switch, that also passes through 502/503 messages.
gaps.saasBaseRef: apps/web/src/app/signed-in/checkout/checkout.page.ts L81; plans.page.ts L153; shared/api-call.ts bodyMessage L52

gaps.feature: Row-lock concurrency of usage (FOR NO KEY UPDATE on the organization row: two consumes can never both pass one balance; grant-on-read written once under concurrent reads)
gaps.detail: Confirmed. The lock is implemented in /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/db/src/organization/usage.ts: .for('no key update') at line 116 and onConflictDoNothing at line 154. The tests run only through openTestData, which uses pgliteDir 'memory://' (/home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/db/src/testing.ts:15). PGlite has a single connection, so the concurrency tests would pass even without the lock. No test in packages/db/src points at DATABASE_URL (the only references are in config.test.ts), and none checks the emitted SQL (no toSQL or 'no key update' assertion). The real-Postgres race that saas-base's usage.int.spec.ts covered goes untested. Fix: add a DATABASE_URL-gated Postgres variant of openTestData, or assert that the lock clause appears in the generated SQL.

gaps.feature: usage.get output when a capacity metric's limit goes below zero after reversals or a negative adjustment
gaps.detail: Confirmed. In /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/plans/src/usage.ts:116-128, a capacity metric gets limit = granted + purchased, and purchased is not clamped there. Only the consumable branch clamps it, with Math.max(0, purchased). The output schema in /home/luismdev/Projects/arrakit/packages/contract/src/usage.ts:13 requires limit: z.number().int().min(0).nullable(). Purchased can go negative in two ways. First, usage.reverse() (packages/db/src/organization/usage.ts:331) writes negative purchased rows for each metric. settleReversal (apps/api/src/billing/settle-event.ts:85-88) caps each reversal at topUp.cents, but each reversal has its own idempotency key and nothing caps their total per payment intent, so a partial refund followed by a full dispute takes back more than was bought. Second, adjust() accepts any nonzero integer, including negative ones. Once a capacity limit drops below 0, usage.get fails output validation with a 500, and the Settings > Usage page and the Billing usage cards stop loading. Fix: clamp the limit to >= 0 (or relax .min(0)), and cap the total reversed per payment intent.

gaps.feature: OpenAPI document matches the endpoints the API actually serves
gaps.detail: Confirmado. apps/api/src/app.ts:16-31 genera el documento con `servers: [{url:'/api'}]` y las rutas REST del contrato, pero createApp (app.ts:43-62) solo monta `RPCHandler` en /api/rpc/*; en apps/api/src no hay ningún `OpenAPIHandler`. health.test.ts comprueba que `/api/health` responde 404 y, a la vez, que el documento usa el servidor /api. Por tanto, todas las operaciones documentadas dan 404. Arreglo: montar `OpenAPIHandler` (@orpc/openapi/fetch) bajo /api, dejando /health fuera, o dejar de anunciar servers:/api y las rutas REST. Añadir un test que llame a una ruta documentada.

gaps.feature: Cron schedules catch up one missed tick (jobs.schedule)
gaps.detail: Confirmado. En packages/db/src/jobs/pg-boss.ts:50, `boss.schedule(name, cron, data, { tz: 'UTC' })` no pasa `missed: 'once'`. pg-boss 12.38 (plans.d.ts, SCHEDULE_MISSED_POLICIES) tiene `skip` por defecto, mientras que types.ts:26 documenta 'missed ticks run once'. Además, defineQueue llama a `boss.updateQueue(name, options)` sobre una cola que ya existe y sobrescribe su política de reintentos. Hoy el impacto es latente, porque ningún código de producción programa un cron.

gaps.feature: Real-Postgres / pg-boss / S3 integration coverage of the data layer
gaps.detail: Confirmado. Ningún fichero *.test.ts de packages/ ni de apps/ prueba pg-boss.ts ni usa pglite-socket o un DATABASE_URL real. Solo lint-guard.test.ts y storage-purge.test.ts mencionan pg-boss, y ninguno lo ejecuta. Sin cubrir: reintentos con backoff y dead-letter, startAfter, singletonKey/sendOnce, el rechazo de exclusive, schedule, la ruta node-postgres de connection.ts (lock advisory, reconexión), URLs firmadas de S3 (403 si no están firmadas o han caducado) y la espera por lock de fila entre conexiones (PGlite trabaja con una sola conexión).

gaps.feature: Local/dev storage fallback parity (signed URLs, content type)
gaps.detail: Confirmado. En packages/db/src/storage/local.ts:33-35 y 59-61, putUrl y getUrl lanzan '[data] local storage does not presign URLs'. `put(name, bytes)` descarta el contentType y `copy` no lo conserva. memoryStorage sí guarda el contentType, pero ningún test comprueba que se conserve al leer ni al copiar. Hoy el impacto es latente, porque ninguna ruta de producción usa putUrl ni getUrl.

gaps.feature: Sign-in links never exposed outside logs (dev mailer)
gaps.detail: Confirmado. Sin RESEND_API_KEY y con NODE_ENV distinto de production, createMailer (apps/api/src/mail/mailer.ts:50-57) crea un outbox en memoria. dev-outbox.ts:7 lo sirve sin autenticación en GET y DELETE /api/dev/outbox. Cualquier entorno no productivo, por ejemplo un staging con NODE_ENV=development, deja leer los magic links de cualquiera. Hay que activarlo solo con un flag explícito (E2E o DEV_OUTBOX) y añadir un test de que la ruta no existe cuando el flag no está puesto.
